name: Perast Waterfront and Old Town
tagline: Baroque palazzos along a car-free promenade
description: The heart of Perast: a slender pedestrian waterfront of honey-stone palazzos, churches, and campaniles facing the two islets. Days here are slow and scenic, with boats, cafes, and seafood terraces steps from your door and cars kept to the town's edge.
bestFor: Couples and slow-travelers who want the view at their doorstep
pros: Best restaurants and boat trips on hand

name: Upper Lanes toward St Elijah
tagline: Quiet stone steps above the bay
description: Climbing the slope behind the waterfront, these narrow lanes and staircases rise toward Mount St Elijah. Stays here are calmer and often better value, trading the promenade's bustle for elevated views, more privacy, and a short, steep walk down into town.
bestFor: Quiet-seekers wanting views and value over foot traffic

name: Kotor Old Town
tagline: The walled town with real amenities
description: A UNESCO-listed medieval walled town about 15 minutes down the bay, Kotor offers what Perast lacks: more restaurants, bars, shops, coworking, and nightlife, plus a dramatic fortress climb. A practical, livelier base within easy reach of Perast's calm.
bestFor: Nomads wanting amenities and buzz near the bay

name: Tivat and Dobrota
tagline: Modern marina and easy bayside living
description: Tivat, home to the Porto Montenegro marina and the closest airport, and Dobrota, the long waterfront stretch just outside Kotor, offer more modern apartments, supermarkets, and everyday convenience along the bay, a practical alternative to Perast's small-town limits.
bestFor: Those prioritizing convenience, flights, and modern stays
